To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
non-muscle (nm) myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK) is a critical mediator of thrombin-induced lung inflammation.
nmMLCK is a critical mediator of EC inflammation and PMN infiltration in response to intravascular thrombin challenge.

(1) nmMLCK is a critical mediator of thrombin-induced lung inflammation; (2) nmMLCK controls nuclear translocation and RelA/p65 transcriptional activity in EC; (3) nmMLCK regulates ICAM-1 transcription in response to thrombin in EC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which thrombin regulates lung inflammation.
the role of thrombin and nmMLCK in the pathogenesis of lung inflammation.
the pathogenesis of acute respiratory distress syndrome, a life threatening condition of the lung.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study by Wang et al. demonstrates the role of nonmuscle myosin in lung inflammation associated with acute intravascular thrombin challenge.
the results from our study indicate the importance of non-muscular myosin light-chain kinase in lung inflammation associated with thrombin-mediated intravascular co-agulation.
thrombin-induced EC inflammation is a critical step in lung PMN recruitment during ALI and that this inflammatory process is regulated by nmMLCK.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thrombin induces lung neutrophil infiltration via nmMLCK-dependent ICAM-1 upregulation and that nmMLCK is a critical target for modulating lung inflammation.
thrombin induces lung PMN infiltration by activating endothelial cells via nmMLCK.
thrombin-induced lung PMN infiltration involves a key role of non-muscule myosin light kinase (nmMLC).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the non-muscle isoform of myosin light-chain kinase (nmMLC) is a key regulator of endothelial cell (endothelial cells) inflammatory response.
non-muscle Myosins play a key role in the inflammatory response to thrombin in the lung, and that this role is mediated by the Myosin Light chain kinase.
thrombin-induced inflammation in the lung requires nmMLCK, which in turn controls the nuclear translocation and activation of RelA/p-65, a key regulator of inflammation.
